Subject: Fabrica — MSA + Order Form redlines (IP + training)

Avery,

Attached are Fabrica's redlines to the MSA and Order Form. High level summary of our asks:  
- Customer needs clear ownership of outputs generated from our data and content (assignment language requested).
- No training on customer-provided data without explicit opt-in (we propose explicit opt-out by default).
- Feedback license should be scoped narrowly: allow Redwood to use anonymized feedback to debug and operate, but not to incorporate verbatim customer content into models used by others.
- Evidence & auditability: we want a retention schedule and the ability to request logs showing whether our data was used for model training.

We highlighted the clauses and added suggested language in the attached doc (Fabrica_MSA_redline_v2.docx). Can you confirm a timeline for legal review and whether Redwood is open to the carveouts above? We need to present a version to procurement by next week.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Fabrica — MSA + Order Form redlines (IP + training)

Folks — quick legal read (high-level + recommended approach):

Summary of key commercial/legal tension
- Fabrica is pushing for assignment of outputs. That is atypical for our standard MSA; assignment implies transfer of title which creates broad operational and downstream risks.
- They want a training opt-out by default and evidence/auditability for training decisions.
- Feedback license carve-in: limited use for debugging/ops vs. broader rights to incorporate content into models.

Recommended compromise we should propose to Fabrica
1) Output ownership: Accept customer ownership of "Customer Content" and ownership of Outputs that are direct transformations of that content for their internal use. Clarify that Redwood retains a limited service license (non-exclusive, worldwide) to store, cache, and process Outputs for the purpose of providing the service (e.g., debugging, serving the model back to the same customer). Add an explicit prohibition on assignment of Outputs to third parties.

2) Training/data use: Agree to opt-out default for training on customer-provided data. Implement operational controls: a per-account training-flag and a documented retention/segregation process. Offer a mechanism for Fabrica to opt in explicitly for a mutually agreed scope and term (and commercial uplift).

3) Feedback license: Narrow the license to "use for service improvement and debugging" and add language that any incorporation of customer content into underlying models used by others requires explicit consent and a separate agreement. Add a telemetry retention schedule and limit to aggregated/non-identifiable usage metrics.

4) Evidence & auditability: Provide a documented proof-of-process: (a) a standard evidence packet showing whether a given datum was used for training (logs and timestamps), subject to reasonable redaction; (b) an SLA for producing such evidence (e.g., 30 business days) and scope limitations for PII. If Fabrica requires on-site audit or extensive forensic logs beyond that, treat as a paid add-on.

5) Contract language edits (next steps): I will produce a tracked change redline that: remove the term "assignment" from Outputs, replace with "ownership of Customer Content and Outputs as defined; limited service license retained by Redwood"; add an explicit training-opt-out clause in the Order Form; narrow feedback license to listed permitted uses.

Action items
- Marissa: will send tracked redline by EOD today (Redwood_proposed_redline_Fabrica_MSA.docx).
- Avery: coordinate with Fabrica on whether procurement has a hard deadline and confirm any non-negotiable clause.
- Ben: prepare a brief pricing uplift option for training opt-in (commercial talking points).

Notes on risk: we should not accept broad assignment or irrevocable transfer of model weights or derivatives. We can accept customer ownership for outputs that's scoped to their content and internal productization; any customer-requested model retraining that uses their data should be commercial and documented.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Fabrica — MSA + Order Form redlines (IP + training)

Kelly — thanks again for the clear redline. After an internal review (see Marissa's notes below) here's a pragmatic proposal we can put in tracked changes. We believe it addresses Fabrica's commercial needs while protecting both parties and keeping the path to procurement short.

Inline summary of our proposed compromises:
- Outputs: Fabrica will have ownership of Outputs that are the direct result of Fabrica-provided Customer Content for Fabrica's internal productization and use. Redwood will retain a limited service license to process, cache and serve those Outputs as necessary to provide the service (explicitly non-assignable to third parties).

- Training: Default = no training on Customer Content. We will implement an account-level training flag. If Fabrica opts in to allow their data to be used to improve models, that opt-in will be governed by a separate scope/term and commercial arrangement.

- Feedback license: Redwood may use feedback and telemetry for debugging and service improvement in aggregate and non-identifiable form. Any use that would incorporate identifiable Fabrica content into models used by other customers requires explicit written consent.

- Evidence & audits: Redwood will provide an evidence packet showing whether a specific dataset was used for training within 30 business days, subject to reasonable PII redactions. On-site audits or deep forensic extractions are out of scope and can be provided as a professional services engagement.

Next steps:
1) Attached tracked redline (Redwood_proposed_redline_Fabrica_MSA.docx) with the edited clauses.
2) If Fabrica agrees to the compromises above, we can finalize and send a signature-ready Order Form via DocuSign by next Tuesday.
3) Ben will follow up on pricing uplift for opt-in training and scope options.

If you see any material concerns, point them out and we will escalate. Otherwise, please confirm that the above approach is acceptable and we'll send the tracked document.

Best,
